shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures rose on Tuesday, buoyed by an oil price rally and firmer spot rubber prices in key producing regions, although a stronger yen capped the advance.($1 = 153.4500 yen)($1 = 6.7108 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures rose on Tuesday, buoyed by an oil price rally and firmer spot rubber prices in key producing regions, although a stronger yen capped the advance.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was up 3.7 yen, or 0.85%, at 440.3 yen ($2.87) per kg, as of 0145 GMT.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 415 yuan, or 2.17%, to 19,525 yuan ($2,909.49) per metric ton, touching its highest since October 8, 2024.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 65 yuan, or 0.42%, to 15,650 yuan per metric ton.

The price of Thailand's benchmark export-grade smoked rubber sheet (RSS3) (RUB-RSS3C-BKK) and block rubber (RUB-STR20C-BKK) were up 0.8% and 0.01%, to stand at 92.28 baht per kg and 81.77 baht per kg, respectively.
Rising raw material prices in major producing areas have lent significant support to spot costs, feeding through to gains in futures, analysts from broker Tianfeng Futures said in a note.

Oil prices extended gains on Tuesday as risks of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East grew after Iran threatened to retaliate against any new U.S. attacks on its assets, heightening worries over supply disruption.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.

climbed to seven-month highs against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, as traders continued to unwind short positions on growing expectations of a Bank of Japan interest rate hike while the dollar was subdued ahead of CPI data this week.
A stronger currency makes yen-denominated assets less affordable to overseas buyers.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 245.4 U.S. cents per kg, up 1.9%, hitting its highest this year.
